skill.name: wunderui-setup
skill.description: Set up WunderUI in an existing React project with Tailwind v4. Detect dependencies, configure styles and MCP, create a probe component, and document setup results.
skill.summary: Configure WunderUI packages, design references, styles, MCP integration, and a visual verification component.
skill.author: wunder-ui

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are formatting, regular expression matching, or expected project file access. Confirmed command execution risks include shell interpolation of checkout paths and npm output. Additional risks include unverified persistent agent rules, an unpinned MCP launcher, and package execution during checkout dry runs; no malicious payload was found.

remediation.issue: Checkout and project paths enter a shell command, and npm output becomes an unquoted installation argument.
remediation.suggestion: Use execFileSync with argument arrays for npm pack and install. Validate the returned archive basename and verify its location before installation.

remediation.issue: Downloaded or locally supplied instruction text is automatically inserted into persistent agent rules.
remediation.suggestion: Require review and explicit approval before inserting instructions. Pin trusted artifacts, verify integrity, and keep unreviewed references separate from agent rules.

remediation.issue: Checkout installation creates files and runs npm pack before honoring --dry.
remediation.suggestion: Check --dry before directory creation or subprocess execution. Print the proposed pack and install operations without running lifecycle scripts.

remediation.issue: The MCP configuration launches an unpinned package through npx -y.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed MCP release and require approval before registering it. Prefer a verified local installation over automatic package retrieval.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified References Become Persistent Agent Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The helper fetches mutable instruction files and inserts their contents into CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md. Compromised references could persistently redirect future agent behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The download-to-rules pipeline has no integrity verification or content approval step. No malicious instruction payload was found in the audited files.

semantic_findings.title: Checkout Dry Runs Execute Package Operations
semantic_findings.description: Despite the documented write-free --dry option, checkout installation creates .wunderui and executes npm pack before checking DRY. Package lifecycle scripts can run during preview.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Directory creation and execSync precede the DRY guard unconditionally in the checkout branch. npm pack can run lifecycle hooks unless scripts are disabled.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned MCP Package Executes Through Agent Configuration
semantic_findings.description: Without a local MCP entrypoint, generated editor configuration launches npx -y wunderui-mcp without a version pin. A changed registry release can execute when loaded.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The generated command accepts automatic package retrieval and specifies no reviewed version. No malicious package release or actual execution was observed.

content.user_title: Set Up WunderUI in Your React Project
content.value_statement: WunderUI components can appear unstyled when package installation, Tailwind scanning, or token precedence is incomplete. This skill coordinates setup, creates a verification component, and documents remaining checks.
actual_capabilities: Detect React frameworks, Tailwind versions, CSS entry files, existing color tokens, and the selected WunderUI plan.
Reuse an installed package, pack a built local checkout, or install @wunderui/react through npm.
Copy design references into .wunderui and insert an instruction block into an existing or newly created agent file.
Register a local or npm-based WunderUI MCP server for Claude Code and detected Cursor or VS Code configurations.
Add the WunderUI stylesheet import and relative Tailwind source path, with optional removal of selected starter style defaults.
Generate a Card, Button, Badge, and Input probe component, then write a Markdown setup report.
limitations: Requires Node.js 20 or newer, an existing project package.json, React, and Tailwind v4 for supported styling.
Browser rendering and MCP tool availability require separate verification; generating files does not prove successful setup.
Checkout installation can execute npm pack and create files even with --dry.
Downloaded agent rules and the unpinned MCP package require independent trust review before use.

prompt_templates.prompt: Review my built WunderUI checkout before setup. Check shell arguments, lifecycle scripts, and MCP version trust; require approval before execution and report remaining checks.

output_examples.input: Check whether my Tailwind v3 project is ready for WunderUI.
output: Readiness: Tailwind v3 does not meet the supported styling requirement.
Next action: approve a Tailwind v4 upgrade before continuing setup.
Verification: a styled WunderUI probe remains pending.

output_examples.input: Summarize setup after creating the probe and registering MCP.
output: Setup report: lists the detected framework, CSS entry, package information, and recorded changes.
Browser check: confirm the probe button background is not transparent.
MCP check: restart the editor and call get_library_info.
Remaining work: confirm token precedence before building the first screen.

best_practices: Review dependency sources, lifecycle scripts, downloaded rules, and the MCP launcher before approving execution.
Run detection first, confirm Tailwind v4, and agree on token precedence before editing the CSS entry.
Keep a recoverable project snapshot, inspect changes, and verify both the probe rendering and MCP availability.
anti_patterns: Treating --dry checkout installation as a guarantee that no subprocesses run or files change.
Automatically trusting downloaded instruction files or an unpinned MCP package.
Removing project token overrides or declaring setup complete without consent and browser verification.

faq.question: Does this create a React project from nothing?
faq.answer: No. The helper requires an existing package.json and checks for React dependencies before the workflow proceeds.

faq.question: Can I use Tailwind v3?
faq.answer: No. The workflow requires Tailwind v4 and stops to offer an upgrade when it detects v3.

faq.question: Can I use a local Core or Pro checkout?
faq.answer: Yes. A built checkout can supply a packed React package and a local MCP entrypoint. Review it before running package operations.

faq.question: Will setup preserve my existing design tokens?
faq.answer: The workflow asks which tokens should take precedence. Project overrides should follow the WunderUI import when you want to preserve them.

faq.question: Why are MCP tools unavailable after registration?
faq.answer: Restart the agent or editor to load the server. A local checkout may also need its MCP dependencies installed.

faq.question: Is dry mode guaranteed to avoid changes?
faq.answer: No. Checkout installation creates a directory and runs npm pack before checking --dry. Use source review for a nonexecuting installation assessment.
